paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in Esther 2. Nobody in this chapter is in charge of their own story. Esther is taken to the palace (Esther 2:8). A king picks a queen from a line of women. And yet things keep falling into place around her, and that's no accident.

Look at the quiet stuff, because that's where the lesson lives. Esther "did not reveal her people or her lineage, because Mordecai had instructed her not to do so" (Esther 2:10). Even as queen, she "obeyed Mordecai's command, as she had done under his care" (Esther 2:20). I think that tells us a crown can change your address without changing your heart, and being faithful in the small, ordinary stuff is what the chapter is built on.

Then watch Mordecai. He sits at the gate, hears about a plot, and reports it. It gets "recorded in the Book of the Chronicles in the presence of the king" (Esther 2:23). So here's the takeaway, baker: the faithful thing you do today may feel small and unseen, but the story isn't over. This one is only getting warmed up, and I'm telling you, keep your oven ready.
